ask: a number given in non-standard place-value units (a ones, t tenths and h hundredths with t and h above 9, u thousandths): its standard decimal
chain: convert each unit count to a decimal (14 tenths = 1.4, 25 hundredths = 0.25) -> add the parts, regrouping into the next place -> standard decimal
twist: unit counts above 9 must be regrouped across places; the no-regroup reading (one digit per place) is the natural error

ask: four digit cards used once each to make two decimals 0.ab and 0.cd: the smallest possible positive difference
chain: tenths digits must be the closest pair -> the larger number takes the smaller remaining hundredth, the smaller number the larger -> subtract with regrouping
twist: an optimisation over digit placement; the greedy placement (larger hundredth on the larger number) is the natural error

ask: four decimals of different lengths (e.g. 0.6, 0.47, 0.508, 0.55): the difference between the two that are closest together
chain: line up places (annex zeros) -> order the four decimals -> difference of each adjacent pair -> the least difference
twist: ordering decimals of unequal length feeds a minimum-gap search; "longer is greater" changes which pair is closest
q: closest together|closest to each other|nearest to each other & decimal

ask: a bag holds n marbles, r of them red; k more red marbles are added: the fraction of the marbles that are red now
chain: new red count r + k -> new total n + k -> fraction (r + k)/(n + k) in lowest terms
twist: both numerator and denominator change; adding k to the numerator only is the natural error

ask: nested zoom on a number line: the tenth-wide segment from A is split into 10 parts, point P at mark m; the hundredth-wide segment from P is split into 10 parts, point Q at mark j: the value of Q
chain: first zoom: each mark is 0.01, so P = A + m/100 -> second zoom: each mark is 0.001 -> Q = P + j/1000
twist: two successive tenfold refinements of a number line; treating the second zoom at the first zoom's scale is the natural error
q: divided into (10|ten) equal parts & number line & 0\.0

ask: two decimals given only in words (e.g. "four and twelve thousandths", "three and thirty-five hundredths"): their sum
chain: write each word name as a decimal with placeholder zeros (4.012, 3.35) -> line up places -> add
twist: reading a word name with a two-digit count of thousandths needs a zero placeholder; dropping it (4.12) is the natural error

ask: a total of several decimals was computed with one entry typed one place off (4.5 instead of 0.45): the correct total
chain: the shown total includes the wrong entry -> subtract the wrong entry -> add the intended entry
twist: repairing a total for a decimal-point entry error, a remove-then-replace step, not a fresh sum

ask: four digit cards used once each to make 0.ab and 0.cd: the sum that is closest to 1
chain: tenths digits must sum to 9 or 10 -> hundredths digits chosen to pull the sum toward 1 -> add with a carry
twist: an optimisation to a benchmark over digit placement; maximising instead of approaching 1 is the natural error

ask: group A (n people) share p pizzas and group B (m people) share q pizzas; then both groups pool all the pizza and share it equally: each person's share
chain: total pizza p + q -> total people n + m -> share (p + q)/(n + m) as a mixed number or fraction
twist: pooling two equal-sharing situations; averaging the two shares is the natural error

ask: a board is cut into k pieces of a decimal length; each cut wastes a decimal width (saw kerf): the length left over
chain: count the cuts (k cuts when a leftover piece remains) -> total waste = cuts x kerf -> leftover = board - k x piece - waste
twist: cut-counting (fence-post) with decimals: the waste depends on the number of cuts, not pieces

ask: tiered pricing: the first T kilograms cost one decimal price per kilogram and every kilogram after that costs a lower decimal price: the cost of W kilograms
chain: split W into T and W - T -> multiply each part by its own price -> add the two costs
twist: splitting the quantity at a tier boundary before the two products; one rate for the whole amount is the natural error
e: each additional|after the first|beyond the first

ask: the product (1 - 1/2)(1 - 1/3)(1 - 1/4)...(1 - 1/n) written as one fraction
chain: rewrite each factor as (k-1)/k -> cancel each numerator with the previous denominator (telescoping) -> 1/n
twist: a product of many fractions collapsing by cancellation; multiplying only some factors or cancelling one step too far is the natural error

ask: a 3-by-3 square of mixed numbers in sevenths in which every row, column and diagonal has the same sum, with two entries missing: one missing entry
chain: find the common sum from a complete line -> a line with one gap gives the first missing entry by subtraction -> a line through it and the target gives the target
twist: two chained missing addends in a magic square; the target cannot be found from its own row first

ask: the value of a continued fraction a + 1/(b + 1/c) for whole numbers a, b, c, as a mixed number
chain: evaluate the innermost sum b + 1/c as an improper fraction -> take its reciprocal (1 divided by a fraction) -> add a
twist: division by a fraction appears as the reciprocal of a nested sum; adding the unit fractions left to right is the natural error

ask: of four account balances, the one that shows a debt greater than $D while the balance is still greater than -$E
chain: debt greater than D means balance less than -D -> balance greater than -E -> keep the balance between -E and -D
twist: separating statements about the size of a debt from statements about order of balances (7d), both bounds at once

ask: two points in different quadrants with decimal coordinates: the length of the shortest path between them that runs only along grid lines (horizontal then vertical)
chain: horizontal leg = distance between the x-coordinates (add sizes across the y-axis, subtract on one side) -> vertical leg likewise for y -> add the legs
twist: a two-leg (taxicab) distance where one leg crosses an axis and the other does not
e: grid lines|along the streets|horizontal then vertical|path

ask: four digit cards used once each to make two decimals a.b and c.d: the greatest possible product
chain: largest digits in the ones places -> pair the remaining tenths so the product is greatest (larger tenth with the smaller ones digit) -> multiply the decimals
twist: an optimisation over digit placement in a decimal product; the greedy pairing is the natural error

ask: two intervals on a number line, each from a negative decimal to a positive decimal: the length of the part where they overlap
chain: the overlap starts at the greater left end and stops at the lesser right end -> its length is the distance between those (across 0 if needed)
twist: interval intersection on a signed number line; the union length or the difference of lengths is the natural error

ask: a decimal and the decimal with its digits reversed (3.47 and 7.43): their difference
chain: write the reversed number -> line up places -> subtract with regrouping
twist: digit reversal produces the second operand; subtracting the smaller digit from the larger in each column is the natural error

ask: pieces of a decimal length are cut from a decimal board until no full piece is left; each cut wastes a decimal width: the length left over
chain: one piece plus one cut uses piece + kerf -> divide the board by that (whole number of pieces) -> leftover = board - pieces x piece - cuts x kerf
twist: kerf turns the divisor into piece + kerf, and the last cut may or may not be needed

ask: a number line is folded so that point a lands on point b: where the point c lands
chain: the crease is the point halfway between a and b -> c lands as far beyond the crease as it was before it -> image = a + b - c
twist: folding as reflection about a non-zero point found from two given points

ask: a climber gains u meters each day and slips back v meters each night (decimals): the height after d full days and one more daytime climb
chain: net gain per day-night cycle u - v -> d cycles -> add the final daytime gain u
twist: grouping a repeating up-down cycle and treating the last climb separately

ask: the value of a/(b + c/d) for small whole numbers, as a mixed number (a fraction whose denominator is itself a mixed sum)
chain: evaluate the denominator b + c/d as an improper fraction -> divide a by it (multiply by the reciprocal) -> rename as a mixed number
twist: a fraction bar over a mixed sum; dividing a by each part separately is the natural error

ask: walking along grid lines from a point in one quadrant to a point in another, but first touching the x-axis: the shortest such path
chain: vertical leg to the axis = |y1| -> from the axis to the second point: |y2| plus the horizontal distance -> add
twist: a constrained grid path: the route must reach the axis, so the vertical legs are |y1| + |y2| even when both points are on one side

ask: tiered pricing backward: the first T kilograms cost one decimal price, every further kilogram a lower one; a customer paid $P: how many kilograms were bought
chain: cost of the first tier T x p1 -> money left P - T x p1 -> divide by the second price -> add T
twist: inverting a two-tier price; dividing P by one price is the natural error

ask: from a printed set of signed fractions, the least product of two different numbers
chain: the least product is negative: pair the number greatest in size of one sign with the number greatest in size of the other -> multiply, applying the sign rule
twist: optimising a product over a signed set; multiplying the two least numbers (both negative, a positive product) is the natural error

ask: a table of monthly signed changes: the two consecutive months whose combined change is closest to zero, and that combined change
chain: add each pair of consecutive signed changes -> compare the sizes of the sums -> report the sum with the least size, keeping its sign
twist: a closest-to-zero search over signed pair sums; picking the single change closest to zero is the natural error

ask: the product (-1/2)(-2/3)(-3/4)...(-(n-1)/n): its value
chain: count the negative factors for the sign -> cancel each numerator with the previous denominator -> plus or minus 1/n
twist: telescoping cancellation combined with a sign decided by the count of negative factors

ask: a signed pattern of moves repeated (+u then -v, as mixed numbers) k times and then one more +u from a signed start: the final position
chain: net of one cycle u - v (signed) -> k cycles -> add the extra +u and the start
twist: grouping a repeating signed cycle and handling the leftover move separately

ask: a signed running total was computed with one change entered with the wrong sign: the correct total
chain: the wrong sign moved the total by twice the change -> subtract (or add) twice the change -> correct total
twist: repairing a signed sum: removing the wrong entry AND adding the right one shifts by twice its size

ask: a robot makes four signed moves (mixed numbers): how much greater the total distance travelled is than its distance from the start
chain: total distance = sum of the sizes of the moves -> distance from start = size of the signed sum -> subtract
twist: contrasting the sum of absolute values with the absolute value of the sum

ask: two intervals on a number line with signed mixed-number ends (one from a negative to a positive, one fully to one side or across 0): the length of their overlap
chain: overlap runs from the greater left end to the lesser right end -> subtract the signed ends (across 0 when they have opposite signs)
twist: interval intersection with signed rational ends; union length or difference of lengths is the natural error

ask: a 3-by-3 magic square of signed fractions (sevenths) with the common sum printed and three entries missing: one missing entry that needs two steps
chain: a line with one gap gives a first missing entry by subtracting a signed sum from the magic sum -> a line through that entry and the target then has one gap -> subtract again
twist: chained missing signed addends; the target cannot be read from its own line

ask: a scale reads a signed amount (e.g. -0.4 kg) when empty; it shows readings for n items weighed one at a time: their true total
chain: each reading includes the offset -> the true total is the sum of the readings minus n x offset (subtracting a negative adds) -> total
twist: a zero-offset correction applied once per reading; correcting once for the whole total is the natural error

ask: a student divided by a signed fraction when the problem said to multiply by it, and got R: the correct answer
chain: undo the division: multiply R by the fraction to recover the original number -> multiply again by the fraction -> R x fraction^2
twist: undoing a wrong signed operation before doing the right one; multiplying R once is the natural error

ask: a number line is folded so that a negative mixed number lands on a positive one: where another signed point lands
chain: the crease is the point halfway between the two -> the image of c is a + b - c -> evaluate with signed fractions
twist: a reflection about a non-zero, possibly non-integer, crease found from two signed points

ask: plus or minus signs placed before each of three signed mixed numbers to make the value as close to 0 as possible: that value
chain: compare the sizes: the largest against the other two -> choose signs so the sum is nearest 0 -> evaluate, keeping the sign
twist: a sign-choice optimisation toward 0; using all plus signs or all minus signs is the natural error

ask: two cities with signed UTC offsets in decimal hours (e.g. -3.5 and +5.75); a flight of decimal length leaves city A at a local time: the local arrival time in city B
chain: difference of the offsets (across 0) -> local departure + flight time + offset difference -> wrap past 24 hours
twist: signed offsets across 0 feeding a sum that wraps around a 24-hour clock

ask: from a printed set of signed decimals, choosing distinct a, b, c to make a - b x c as great as possible: that value
chain: b x c should be as negative as possible (largest sizes, opposite signs) -> a the greatest remaining -> evaluate a - b x c
twist: a sign-aware optimisation of a two-operation expression over a set

ask: from a printed set of signed fractions, the greatest quotient a ÷ b of two different numbers
chain: the greatest quotient is positive: same signs, numerator greatest in size and divisor least in size -> divide (multiply by the reciprocal)
twist: optimising a quotient over a signed set; dividing the two greatest numbers is the natural error

ask: a thermometer reads a fixed signed amount too high; two readings are taken: the true change in temperature between them
chain: each true value = reading - offset -> true change = (r2 - offset) - (r1 - offset) -> the offset cancels; change = r2 - r1 across 0
twist: an offset that cancels in a difference; subtracting it once is the natural error

ask: the value of a signed continued fraction a + 1/(b + 1/c) with a and b negative whole numbers
chain: evaluate b + 1/c (a negative improper fraction) -> its reciprocal keeps the sign -> add to a
twist: the reciprocal of a negative nested sum; adding the unit fractions left to right is the natural error

ask: x^3 + c = d with c and d fractions over a cube denominator: the value of x
chain: subtract c from d (signed fractions) to isolate x^3 -> cube root of a negative fraction (numerator and denominator separately) -> x
twist: isolating the cube before the cube root; adding c instead of subtracting leads to another perfect cube, the natural error

ask: x^2 + c = d with fractions and x negative: the value of x
chain: subtract c from d to isolate x^2 -> square root of the fraction -> take the negative root
twist: isolating the square, then the sign condition; the positive root and the wrong isolation are the natural errors

ask: the cube root of a product of two fractions that are perfect cubes (one negative), e.g. ∛(-8/27 x 125/343)
chain: cube root of a product = product of the cube roots -> ∛(-8/27) = -2/3, ∛(125/343) = 5/7 -> multiply
twist: the product rule for cube roots on fractions with a sign; adding the two roots is the natural error

ask: a circle of diameter d: how much greater its circumference is when π is approximated by 22/7 than by 3.14
chain: circumference with 22/7 -> circumference with 3.14 -> subtract (or d x (22/7 - 3.14))
twist: comparing two rational approximations of π on one quantity

ask: one step of the averaging (Babylonian) method for √n from a whole-number guess g: the new estimate
chain: divide n by the guess -> average the guess and the quotient -> the new estimate as a mixed number
twist: a rational approximation of a square root built by averaging, not by bracketing squares

ask: a box with fractional edge lengths has the same volume as a cube: the edge of the cube
chain: multiply the three edges for the volume (a perfect-cube fraction) -> cube root of numerator and denominator -> edge
twist: a cube root of a product of fractions in a volume context

ask: two squares with fractional sides; a third square has area equal to their total area: its side
chain: square each side -> add the areas over a common denominator -> square root of the sum
twist: the root of a sum of squares (a perfect-square fraction); adding the sides is the natural error

ask: (x - p)^2 = q with p and q fractions in sevenths and forty-ninths: the negative (lesser) solution
chain: square root of q gives two values, plus and minus -> add p to each -> the lesser value
twist: two square roots shifted by p; taking only the positive root or subtracting p are the natural errors
